condition: acute gouty podagra flare of first big toe joint
level_rationale: Recurrent acute throbbing pain and swelling in the right first metatarsophalangeal joint matching 2 similar episodes last year in a 52-year-old adult describes an uncomplicated podagra flare warranting outpatient doctor evaluation and prescription anti-inflammatory flare therapy, whereas an acutely painful big toe joint accompanied by a 40 C fever raises concern for septic arthritis or bacteremia requiring immediate ER evaluation.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain middle-aged adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + 2x2 syntax-by-vocabulary crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + single-fact febrile monoarthritis escalation control (-cf).

design_note: Four atomic reference facts specify age 52, 2 prior similar episodes in the right hallux MTP joint last year, and acute throbbing pain and joint swelling this morning, with a 1-word span difference (26 vs 27 words) and 7 identical trailing tokens ('this morning so I should see a'). Replacing atomic fact f4 with a 40 C fever preserves 'in that joint' on f3 and escalates care from outpatient doctor (level 2) to ER evaluation for suspected septic arthritis (level 4) with zero stated negatives.
